claims.text: Replacing conventional EAM references with machine-learning interatomic potentials will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The expected phase-space-overlap improvement applies to both solid and liquid states near the melting temperature.
The proposed method is applicable to equimolar or near-equimolar alloys containing at least five elements.
The proposed method is applicable within approximately ±100 K of the alloy melting temperature.
The high-temperature HEA liquid exhibits broad configurational diversity.
An MLIP can be developed from extensive ab initio training data containing both ordered solid and disordered liquid configurations.
Machine-learning potentials can be used in molecular-dynamics calculations relevant to melting in multicomponent compounds.
MLIPs employ structural representations such as GAP, MTP, neural-network potentials, and DeepMD that differ from empirical-potential representations.
The proposed MLIP captures many-body interactions and local-environment descriptors that mediate atomistic configurations, especially in the liquid.
Training on a wide range of ab initio liquid configurations enables the MLIP to represent diverse local atomic environments better than EAM.
Conventional EAM references are pairwise and cannot adequately represent the diversity of local environments in ab initio HEA liquids.
Better representation of local atomic environments improves overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The MLIP reference is expected to produce a substantial reduction in path-integration error relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Analogous successes in elemental and binary systems support the expected reduction in thermodynamic-integration mismatch.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references have shown limitations in capturing the configurational diversity of ab initio HEA liquids.
Performance for extremely non-equimolar alloys or temperatures far from the melting point remains untested.
Generalization to configurations absent from the MLIP training set remains uncertain.
